interpretations: Literal (command validity): only A is a syntactically valid hostnamectl invocation that sets the hostname; C is not hostnamectl syntax and D is not a CLI.

Persistence semantics: the stem demands survival of reboot (static hostname); set-hostname without keys writes pretty+static+transient, the static part living in /etc/hostname, so A satisfies it; B is the transient-only trap.
Alternative-tool reading: Rocky 9 offers several routes (hostnamectl, nmcli general hostname, /etc/hostname, nmtui); only the hostnamectl route is present and A is the only correct entry.
reason: Ambiguity exists only at the level of framing (root/sudo not stated, "static" not named explicitly), not answerability. No interpretation makes a second option defensible: B is transient-only, C is invalid syntax, D is a D-Bus service rather than a command.
